answers.answer: The second segment, d1a14h2 (chain H residues 1-8), is not a protein domain at all. It is an artifact entry: an N-terminal expression/purification tag left on the recombinant NC10 antibody heavy-chain variable region (PDB 1a14 is the NC10 Fv fragment bound to influenza N9 neuraminidase). Its 8-residue length is consistent with an engineered epitope tag such as the FLAG octapeptide (DYKDDDDK); the exact tag identity should be confirmed from the PDB SEQRES/entity records rather than assumed. SCOPe (since 2.06) files such segments under class l ('Artifacts'), fold l.1, superfamily l.1.1, family l.1.1.1 ('Tags'), so d1a14h2 is l.1.1.1. The genuine protein domain is d1a14h1 (residues 9-111), the antibody VH domain, classified in class b (all-beta), fold b.1 (immunoglobulin-like beta-sandwich), superfamily b.1.1 (immunoglobulin), family b.1.1.1 (V set domains, antibody variable domain-like). Similarity to d1a14h2 must NOT be treated as protein homology evidence. Reasons: (1) class l is explicitly a non-evolutionary, non-structural catch-all; SCOPe states these segments are not evolutionarily related to each other or to any true fold/superfamily, so family/superfamily/fold membership in class l carries none of the homology (superfamily) or common-ancestry (family) meaning it has in classes a-g. (2) The sequence is a cloning/vector artifact, not part of the natural gene product, so matches reflect shared laboratory constructs, not descent. (3) Tags are short, low-complexity, and recur across thousands of unrelated PDB entries, so they produce spurious hits in sequence (BLAST/HMM) and structure searches; any alignment that is anchored on residues 1-8 should be masked or discarded. (4) No function, fold, or template inference should be transferred from the tag: it is typically disordered or arbitrarily positioned, carries no neuraminidase-binding or Ig-related function, and must not be used as a modeling template. (5) SCOPe excludes class l domains from the ASTRAL sequence/representative subsets (e.g., 40%/95% identity sets), so d1a14h2 should not be selected as a representative or counted in fold/superfamily statistics. Any homology or template argument for 1a14 chain H should rest solely on d1a14h1 (b.1.1.1), and homology claims to other Ig V-set domains should be made at the appropriate level: shared family b.1.1.1 implies clear common ancestry and conserved antibody-variable architecture, superfamily b.1.1 implies probable common origin among Ig-like domains, while fold-level (b.1) similarity alone does not establish homology. Caveat: statements about the specific tag sequence are from pretrained knowledge and should be verified against the SCOPe 2.08 domain record and PDB entity annotations.
